---
title: "5: Conditional Probability"
---

We have already discussed the idea of conditional probability during our introduction to sample and state spaces. But for our previous problems, while we made to state our assumptions, these were not included directly in the mathematical notation we used.

Consider a state space $\Omega$ with two events, $A$ and $B$.

Now consider that Event $B$ has just occurred. The old universe $\Omega$ is irrelevant. Everything outside of $B$ has ceased to exist. $B$ is the **new universe**.

Now consider that Event $A$ occurs **after we know** event $B$ has occured. The numerator (the physical space of the intersection) has not changed at all. What changed is the denominator: we must re-normalize the new universe so that its total measure equals 1 (Axiom 2 from Week 4).

What we have here is the **Conditional Probability** of Event $A$ given Event $B$ has occured, which in notation is written as $P(A\vert{}B)$.
